hook.line: Mariana is late to the café again, and she doesn't just announce it. She cushions the news with a small opener that says: let me explain what is really going on.
hook.es: Lo que pasa es que mi carro no prende.
hook.en: The thing is my car won't start.

examples.en: The thing is they didn't tell me in time.

rule:
*Lo que pasa es que* means "the thing is…". It cushions an excuse, an explanation or bad news. Without it, the next sentence can sound blunt.

It is one fixed block, then an ordinary full sentence in the tense you need: *Lo que pasa es que no tengo tiempo*; *Lo que pasa es que llegué tarde*.

The opener itself stays in the present, *pasa*.

The chattier, shorter cousin is *Es que…*
smallPrint: Teachers call this a pseudo-cleft: *lo que* + verb + *ser* puts the explanation at the end, where it lands.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *es que* or *es de*: Lo que pasa ___ el taller está cerrado. Type the whole sentence.
yourTurn.answer: Lo que pasa es que el taller está cerrado.
yourTurn.why: After the block comes *que* and a full sentence.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *pasa* or *pasó*: Lo que ___ es que no tengo tiempo. Type the whole sentence.
yourTurn.answer: Lo que pasa es que no tengo tiempo.
yourTurn.why: The opener stays in the present: *pasa*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: The thing is my car won't start.
yourTurn.answer: Lo que pasa es que mi carro no prende.
yourTurn.why: The opener, then the plain news.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: The thing is they didn't tell me in time.
yourTurn.answer: Lo que pasa es que no me avisaron a tiempo.
yourTurn.why: *Avisaron* is "they told", and *me* goes before it.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: The thing is I arrived late.
yourTurn.answer: Lo que pasa es que llegué tarde.
yourTurn.why: The news is in the past, so *llegué*; the opener stays in the present.

yourTurn.prompt: Soften it with *lo que pasa es que*: *Vale no está.*
yourTurn.answer: Lo que pasa es que Vale no está.
yourTurn.why: Put the opener in front and keep the rest as it was.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: The thing is the boss has already made the decision.
yourTurn.answer: Lo que pasa es que el jefe ya tomó la decisión.
yourTurn.why: *Ya tomó* says it is already done.

pitfalls.wrong: Lo que pasa que no tengo tiempo.
pitfalls.right: Lo que pasa es que no tengo tiempo.
pitfalls.why: Almost. Don't drop the *es*: the block is *lo que pasa es que*.

pitfalls.wrong: Qué pasa es que el carro no prende.
pitfalls.right: Lo que pasa es que el carro no prende.
pitfalls.why: Almost. "What" here is *lo que*; *qué* alone asks a question.

pitfalls.wrong: Lo que pasa es que no tengas tiempo.
pitfalls.right: Lo que pasa es que no tengo tiempo.
pitfalls.why: Almost. You are stating a fact, so use the ordinary present: *tengo*.

personal: Think of something you would have to explain to a friend, like why you are late or can't come. Start with *Lo que pasa es que…*
